desk_read: Energy short covering dominated the session, with WTI surging +3.82% on volume 1.3x its 20-day average while total open interest fell -776 contracts, the clearest price-up, OI-down short-covering signature on the board. Brent told the same story at +2.80%, and deepening backwardation in both curves underlines how tight nearby supply reads to the market. Equities were the mirror image: the S&P 500 slipped -0.58% and Nasdaq 100 -0.08% on long liquidation with volume 1.3x average in both, leaving equity longs looking fragile at elevated volume. Gold saw the most decisive exit, with total open interest off -2.9k contracts and volume 1.4x its 20-day average on a -1.29% decline, a clean long-liquidation signature worth watching if energy strength persists.
oil_read: Both WTI and Brent surged on short covering, with volume running at 1.3x and 1.1x respective 20-day averages, suggesting the move was largely driven by defensive buying rather than fresh longs. WTI total open interest slipped -776 contracts (-0.1%), keeping the flow read fragile; Brent's net open interest was essentially flat (-40 contracts). Both curves remain in backwardation, with WTI's CLZ26-CLK27 spread at +12.25 $/bbl and Brent's BZZ26-BZK27 at +18.36 $/bbl, confirming commercial tightness in nearby delivery.
bias_read: WTI is bullish and Brent mildly bullish, but both moves are driven by short covering rather than fresh conviction — the backwardation steepening supports the upside bias yet warns of limited durability if shorts are already cleared. Copper stands out as the clearest structural signal: a mildly bullish bias built on new longs at above-average volume supports the current move with more staying power than the oil short squeeze. Gold and Silver are both mildly bearish via long liquidation at elevated volume, warning that crowded longs remain at risk of further unwinding. Equities echo that defensive tilt, with S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 both mildly bearish on long liquidation. Across markets, the overall picture skews toward risk-off rotation, with commodity strength in oil and copper offset by pressure on metals and equities.
